subproblems.title: C¹ approximation of Lipschitz functions (Simon Ch. 2, Thm 1.5)
subproblems.statement: Let n ≥ 1 and let f : ℝⁿ → ℝ (ℝⁿ = Rn n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) be Lipschitz with constant K ∈ ℝ≥0. Then for every ε ∈ (0, ∞] there is a C¹ function g : ℝⁿ → ℝ (ContDiff ℝ 1 g) such that the Lebesgue measure (volume) of {x : f(x) ≠ g(x)} is less than ε. (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.5; used for the cited fact (H4) of the parent proof.)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∀ (f : Rn n → ℝ) (K : ℝ≥0), LipschitzWith K f → ∀ ε : ℝ≥0∞, 0 < ε → ∃ g : Rn n → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 g ∧ volume {x | f x ≠ g x} < ε
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 2, printed proof of Theorem 1.5 (C¹ Approximation Theorem: Rademacher, Lusin, Egoroff, Whitney extension 1.6), with details filled in. The book's remarks that Lusin's theorem 'applies to sets of infinite measure for Lⁿ' and that Egoroff is applied 'to the finite measure sets C ∩ B_j(0)' with uniform convergence 'on each bounded subset' are implemented below by working on the open annuli Ann_j.

Notation. ℝⁿ = Rn n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with Lebesgue measure Lⁿ = volume; |·| is the Euclidean norm; B_r(x) is the closed ball and B°_r(x) the open ball. Df(x) := fderiv ℝ f x ∈ L(ℝⁿ, ℝ) (this is 0 where f is not differentiable).

Proof.
0. Reductions. Replacing ε by min(ε, 1) we may assume that 0 < ε ≤ 1 is a real number. For j ∈ ℕ let Ann_j := {x : j < |x| < j + 1} (open and bounded) and ε_j := ε·2^(−j−3), so that Σ_j ε_j = ε/4. Every x with |x| ∉ ℕ lies in exactly one Ann_j, and each sphere {|x| = j} is Lⁿ-null because n ≥ 1 (Measure.addHaar_sphere). Df is Borel measurable (measurable_fderiv), so are its components x ↦ Df(x)e_i, i = 1, …, n (measurable_fderiv_apply_const), and ‖Df(x)‖ ≤ K for every x (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz).
1. Rademacher. B := {x : f is differentiable at x} is Borel (measurableSet_of_differentiableAt) and Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ B) = 0 (LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt).
2. Lusin on annuli. Fix j and let S_j := Ann_j ∩ B, a Borel set of finite measure. Lebesgue measure is regular, so every Borel set of finite measure contains closed subsets of almost full measure (MeasurableSet.exists_isClosed_diff_lt); this is the regularity hypothesis of SimonGMT's finite-measure Lusin theorem Chapter01.exists_isClosed_continuousOn_of_measurable. Applying it with ν = volume and A = S_j to each component x ↦ Df(x)e_i with tolerance ε_j/n gives closed sets C_{j,i} ⊆ S_j with Lⁿ(S_j ∖ C_{j,i}) < ε_j/n such that x ↦ Df(x)e_i is continuous on C_{j,i}. Put C_j := ⋂_{i=1}^n C_{j,i}. Then C_j is closed, C_j ⊆ S_j, Lⁿ(S_j ∖ C_j) < ε_j, and Df is continuous on C_j (continuousOn_clm_apply: a map into L(ℝⁿ, ℝ) is continuous on a set iff all its evaluations are). C_j is compact and contained in the open annulus Ann_j, hence there is δ_j > 0 with j + δ_j ≤ |x| ≤ j + 1 − δ_j for all x ∈ C_j.
3. Gluing. Let C := ⋃_j C_j. Every point of ℝⁿ has a neighbourhood meeting only finitely many Ann_j, hence only finitely many C_j; so the family (C_j) is locally finite and C is closed (LocallyFinite.isClosed_iUnion). If x ∈ C_j, then B°_{δ_j}(x) ∩ C = B°_{δ_j}(x) ∩ C_j, because the points of B°_{δ_j}(x) have norm in (j, j + 1); hence Df restricted to C is continuous at x. Moreover C ⊆ B, and ℝⁿ ∖ C ⊆ (ℝⁿ ∖ B) ∪ ⋃_j {|x| = j} ∪ ⋃_j (S_j ∖ C_j), so Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ C) ≤ 0 + 0 + Σ_j ε_j = ε/4.
4. Whitney quotients. For x ≠ y set R(x, y) := (f(y) − f(x) − Df(x)(y − x))/|y − x|. For k ≥ 1 define σ_k(x) := sup{|R(x, y)| : y ∈ C, 0 < |y − x| < 1/k} for x ∈ C (with sup ∅ := 0), and σ_k(x) := 0 for x ∉ C.
 (a) 0 ≤ σ_k ≤ 2K, because |f(y) − f(x)| ≤ K|y − x| and ‖Df(x)‖ ≤ K.
 (b) σ_k(x) → 0 as k → ∞ for every x ∈ C: since x ∈ B, for every η > 0 there is δ > 0 with |R(x, y)| ≤ η whenever 0 < |y − x| < δ, so σ_k(x) ≤ η as soon as 1/k ≤ δ.
 (c) σ_k is Borel measurable. Let D₀ ⊆ C be countable and dense in C (C is a separable metric space; TopologicalSpace.exists_countable_dense). For fixed x, the map y ↦ R(x, y) is continuous on ℝⁿ ∖ {x} (f is continuous), and {y ∈ C : 0 < |y − x| < 1/k} is relatively open in C, hence D₀ is dense in it; therefore σ_k(x) = sup{|R(x, y)| : y ∈ D₀, 0 < |y − x| < 1/k} for x ∈ C. For each fixed y ∈ D₀ the function x ↦ 1_C(x)·1_{0<|y−x|<1/k}(x)·|R(x, y)| is Borel (f continuous, Df Borel, indicators of Borel sets). Hence σ_k is a countable supremum of Borel functions bounded by 2K, so it is Borel measurable and strongly measurable.
5. Egorov and inner regularity. Fix j. C_j is Borel of finite measure, every σ_k is strongly measurable, and σ_k → 0 at every point of C_j. By Egorov's theorem (MeasureTheory.tendstoUniformlyOn_of_ae_tendsto) there is a Borel t_j ⊆ C_j with Lⁿ(t_j) ≤ ε_j such that σ_k → 0 uniformly on A'_j := C_j ∖ t_j. By inner regularity choose a closed A_j ⊆ A'_j with Lⁿ(A'_j ∖ A_j) < ε_j; A_j is compact and A_j ⊆ C_j ⊆ Ann_j. Let A := ⋃_j A_j. As in step 3 the family (A_j) is locally finite, so A is closed; A ⊆ C; and since ℝⁿ ∖ A ⊆ (ℝⁿ ∖ C) ∪ ⋃_j (t_j ∪ (A'_j ∖ A_j)), we get Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ A) ≤ ε/4 + Σ_j ε_j + Σ_j ε_j = 3ε/4 < ε. Finally, a compact Q ⊆ A is contained in B_J(0) for some J ∈ ℕ, hence in A_0 ∪ … ∪ A_J; therefore σ_k → 0 uniformly on Q.
6. Whitney's hypothesis 1.6(*). We verify SimonGMT's structure Chapter02.HasWhitneyC1Compatibility A f Df. (continuous_value) f is continuous on A. (continuous_derivative) Df is continuous on A, since A ⊆ C (step 3). (remainder) Given a compact Q ⊆ A and η > 0, choose k with σ_k ≤ η on Q (step 5) and put δ := 1/k. For x ∈ Q and y ∈ A with |x − y| < δ, either y = x (and the remainder vanishes) or y ∈ C with 0 < |y − x| < 1/k, so |f(y) − f(x) − Df(x)(y − x)| = |R(x, y)|·|y − x| ≤ σ_k(x)|y − x| ≤ η|y − x|.
7. Whitney extension (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.6; SimonGMT Chapter02.exists_contDiff_one_extension_of_whitney, applicable since A is closed) yields g : ℝⁿ → ℝ with ContDiff ℝ 1 g and g = f on A. Then {x : f(x) ≠ g(x)} ⊆ ℝⁿ ∖ A, so Lⁿ({f ≠ g}) < ε. ∎

Rademacher: f is differentiable off a Borel Lⁿ-null set
Lusin (SimonGMT finite-measure version, Lebesgue regularity) for each component of Df on Ann_j ∩ B: closed C_j with Df|C_j continuous and small loss
C = ⋃ C_j is closed (locally finite, separated pieces), Df|C continuous, Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ C) ≤ ε/4
Whitney quotients σ_k: bounded by 2K, Borel via a countable dense subset, σ_k → 0 pointwise on C
Egorov + inner regularity on each C_j: closed A ⊆ C with Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ A) < ε and σ_k → 0 uniformly on compact subsets of A
Verify HasWhitneyC1Compatibility A f Df and apply SimonGMT's Whitney extension: g ∈ C¹ with g = f on A

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the parent proof's steps 2a–2f, i.e. Simon Ch. 3, printed proof of Lemma 1.2 ('only if'), with details filled in.

Notation. ℝⁿ = Rn n with Lⁿ = volume; ℝ^{n+ℓ} = Amb n ℓ; Hⁿ = μHE[n]; on ℝⁿ itself Hⁿ = Lⁿ (InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume, finrank ℝⁿ = n). B_r(b) is the closed ball, B°_r(b) the open ball. The sibling c1_approximation states: for n ≥ 1, every Lipschitz h : ℝⁿ → ℝ and every ε > 0 there is a C¹ function g : ℝⁿ → ℝ with Lⁿ({h ≠ g}) < ε.

Proof.
1. Rectifiability data. By the definition of Chapter03.CountablyRectifiable there are M₀ with Hⁿ(M₀) = 0 and maps F_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+ℓ} (j ∈ ℕ), F_j being K_j-Lipschitz, with M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝⁿ). Put N' := n + ℓ ≥ 1 and F_j^q(z) := F_j(z)_q, the q-th coordinate (q = 1, …, N'); each F_j^q is K_j-Lipschitz.
2. C¹ approximation (parent 2b). For i ≥ 1 and each q, the sibling c1_approximation gives a C¹ function g_{ij}^q : ℝⁿ → ℝ with Lⁿ({F_j^q ≠ g_{ij}^q}) < 1/(iN'). Let G_{ij}(z) be the point of ℝ^{n+ℓ} with coordinates (g_{ij}^1(z), …, g_{ij}^{N'}(z)). G_{ij} is C¹, since its coordinates are C¹ and the coordinate identification ℝ^{n+ℓ} ≅ ℝ^{N'} is a continuous linear equivalence. Since {F_j ≠ G_{ij}} ⊆ ⋃_q {F_j^q ≠ g_{ij}^q}, we get Lⁿ({F_j ≠ G_{ij}}) < 1/i.
3. The sets Z_j. Z_j := ⋂_{i≥1} {F_j ≠ G_{ij}} satisfies Lⁿ(Z_j) ≤ 1/i for all i, so Lⁿ(Z_j) = 0. By the Lipschitz image bound (SimonGMT Chapter02.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn) and Hⁿ = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ, Hⁿ(F_j(Z_j)) ≤ K_jⁿ·Lⁿ(Z_j) = 0. If z ∉ Z_j then F_j(z) = G_{ij}(z) for some i; hence F_j(ℝⁿ) ⊆ F_j(Z_j) ∪ ⋃_i G_{ij}(ℝⁿ).
4. Critical sets (parent 2c). Let C_{ij} := {b : DG_{ij}(b) is not injective} and O_{ij} := ℝⁿ ∖ C_{ij}. O_{ij} is open: it is the preimage of the open set of injective linear maps (ContinuousLinearMap.isOpen_injective) under the continuous map b ↦ DG_{ij}(b) (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv). Since G_{ij} is differentiable everywhere, C_{ij} = {b : G_{ij} is differentiable at b and DG_{ij}(b) is not injective}, so SimonGMT Chapter02.area_image_criticalSet_eq_zero gives Hⁿ(G_{ij}(C_{ij})) = 0.
5. Local lower Lipschitz bound (parent 2d). Fix b ∈ O_{ij} and put L := DG_{ij}(b). L is an injective linear map on the finite-dimensional space ℝⁿ, hence antilipschitz (LinearMap.injective_iff_antilipschitz): there is s_b > 0 with |Lv| ≥ s_b|v| for all v ∈ ℝⁿ. By continuity of DG_{ij} and openness of O_{ij} choose ρ_b > 0 with B_{ρ_b}(b) ⊆ O_{ij} and ‖DG_{ij}(b') − L‖ ≤ s_b/2 for all b' ∈ B_{ρ_b}(b). The C¹ map φ := G_{ij} − L has Dφ = DG_{ij} − L, so the mean value inequality on the convex ball (Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderiv_le) gives |φ(b') − φ(b'')| ≤ (s_b/2)|b' − b''| for b', b'' ∈ B_{ρ_b}(b). Consequently |G_{ij}(b') − G_{ij}(b'')| ≥ |L(b' − b'')| − |φ(b') − φ(b'')| ≥ (s_b/2)|b' − b''| for all b', b'' ∈ B_{ρ_b}(b), in particular on the open ball B°_{ρ_b}(b). Moreover DG_{ij}(b') is injective for every b' ∈ B°_{ρ_b}(b) ⊆ O_{ij}. (The parent reaches the same bound after composing with a coordinate projection z for which z∘L is invertible; s_b plays the role of ‖(D(z∘G_{ij})(b))^(−1)‖^(−1).)
6. Lindelöf (parent 2f). The open balls B°_{ρ_b}(b), b ∈ O_{ij}, cover O_{ij}. ℝⁿ is second countable, so there is a countable T_{ij} ⊆ O_{ij} with O_{ij} = ⋃_{b ∈ T_{ij}} B°_{ρ_b}(b) (TopologicalSpace.isOpen_iUnion_countable).
7. Enumeration. The set of triples (i, j, b) with i ≥ 1, j ∈ ℕ and b ∈ T_{ij} is countable. Enumerate it as k ↦ (i_k, j_k, b_k) and put G_k := G_{i_k j_k}, c_k := b_k, r_k := ρ_{b_k} > 0 and σ_k := s_{b_k}/2 > 0. If there are only finitely many triples (or none), fill the remaining indices with the dummy piece G(z) := (z, 0) ∈ ℝ^{n+ℓ} (first n coordinates z, last ℓ coordinates 0): it is a linear isometric embedding, hence C¹ with injective derivative equal to itself, and c := 0, r := 1, σ := 1 work for it. By step 5 every piece satisfies: DG_k(b) is injective for b ∈ B°_{r_k}(c_k), and σ_k|b₁ − b₂| ≤ |G_k(b₁) − G_k(b₂)| for b₁, b₂ ∈ B°_{r_k}(c_k).
8. The null set. Let Z₀ := toMeasurable Hⁿ (M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(Z_j) ∪ ⋃_{i,j} G_{ij}(C_{ij})). It is Borel, and as a measurable hull of a countable union of Hⁿ-null sets (steps 1, 3, 4) it satisfies Hⁿ(Z₀) = 0.
9. Covering. Let x ∈ M. If x ∈ M₀ then x ∈ Z₀. Otherwise x = F_j(z) for some j and z. If z ∈ Z_j then x ∈ F_j(Z_j) ⊆ Z₀. Otherwise F_j(z) = G_{ij}(z) for some i. If z ∈ C_{ij} then x ∈ G_{ij}(C_{ij}) ⊆ Z₀. Otherwise z ∈ O_{ij}, so z ∈ B°_{ρ_b}(b) for some b ∈ T_{ij}, and x = G_k(z) ∈ G_k(B°_{r_k}(c_k)) for the index k of the triple (i, j, b). Hence M ⊆ Z₀ ∪ ⋃_k G_k(B°_{r_k}(c_k)). ∎

subproblems.title: Embedded C¹ piece: Borel, finite Hⁿ, approximate tangent plane DG(b)(ℝⁿ)
subproblems.statement: Let n, ℓ ≥ 0, G : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+ℓ} of class C¹, c ∈ ℝⁿ, r ∈ ℝ, σ > 0, and B := B°_r(c) (open ball). Assume DG(b) is injective for every b ∈ B and σ|b₁ − b₂| ≤ |G(b₁) − G(b₂)| for all b₁, b₂ ∈ B. Let N := G(B). Then (i) N is Borel; (ii) Hⁿ(N) < ∞ (Hⁿ = μHE[n]); (iii) for every b ∈ B, the subspace P := DG(b)(ℝⁿ) (LinearMap.range of the derivative) is the approximate tangent space of N at G(b) in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.4 (Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N (G b) P): finrank P = n and lim_{λ↓0} ∫_{η_{G(b),λ}(N)} f dHⁿ = ∫_P f dHⁿ for every compactly supported continuous f : ℝ^{n+ℓ} → ℝ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (G : Rn n → Amb n ℓ) (c : Rn n) (r σ : ℝ), ContDiff ℝ 1 G → 0 < σ → (∀ b ∈ ball c r, Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ G b)) → (∀ b₁ ∈ ball c r, ∀ b₂ ∈ ball c r, σ * ‖b₁ - b₂‖ ≤ ‖G b₁ - G b₂‖) → MeasurableSet (G '' ball c r) ∧ (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) (G '' ball c r) < ⊤ ∧ ∀ b ∈ ball c r, Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (G '' ball c r) (G b) (LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ G b).toLinearMap)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the parent proof's step 2e (Borel, finite measure) and step 3 (blow-up of an embedded C¹ piece), with details filled in.

Notation. ℝⁿ = Rn n, ℝ^{n+ℓ} = Amb n ℓ, Hⁿ = μHE[n] (on ℝⁿ, Hⁿ = Lⁿ = volume). B := B°_r(c) (open ball), N := G(B), B_s(y) closed balls. η_{x,λ}(y) := λ^(−1)(y − x) = Chapter03.blowUpMap x λ y. C_c denotes the compactly supported continuous f : ℝ^{n+ℓ} → ℝ. JG(b') := areaJacobianAt G b' = normDet(DG(b')) ≥ 0, a continuous function of b' (SimonGMT Chapter02.continuous_normDet composed with the continuous map DG). Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N x P means: finrank P = n and ∫_{η_{x,λ}(N)} f dHⁿ → ∫_P f dHⁿ as λ ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c.

Proof.
0. If r ≤ 0 then B = ∅, N = ∅, and all three claims are trivial; assume r > 0. The lower bound σ|b₁ − b₂| ≤ |G(b₁) − G(b₂)| on B with σ > 0 shows that G is injective on B.
1. Finite measure. DG is continuous, hence bounded by some Λ on the compact closed ball B_r(c). By the mean value inequality G is Λ-Lipschitz on the convex set B. Therefore Hⁿ(N) ≤ Λⁿ·Hⁿ(B) = Λⁿ·Lⁿ(B) < ∞ (SimonGMT Chapter02.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn; Hⁿ = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ). This is (ii).
2. Borel. B is Borel and G is continuous and injective on B, so N = G(B) is Borel by the Lusin–Souslin theorem (MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn). (Alternatively, B is σ-compact, hence so is N.) This is (i).
3. Fix b ∈ B and put x := G(b), L := DG(b), P := L(ℝⁿ) = LinearMap.range L. Since L is injective, finrank P = finrank ℝⁿ = n (LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj). Fix f ∈ C_c and R > 0 with f = 0 outside B_R(0), and let M_f := sup|f|.
4. Rescaled parametrization (parent 3a). For λ > 0 let B^λ := {z ∈ ℝⁿ : b + λz ∈ B} (an open set) and Γ_λ(z) := λ^(−1)(G(b + λz) − x). Γ_λ is C¹ with DΓ_λ(z) = DG(b + λz), which is injective for z ∈ B^λ; Γ_λ is injective on B^λ (G is injective on B); and Γ_λ(B^λ) = η_{x,λ}(N), because η_{x,λ}(G(b')) = Γ_λ((b' − b)/λ).
5. Area formula (parent 3b). SimonGMT Chapter02.integral_area_formula_of_injective_derivative, applied to Γ_λ on the Borel set B^λ (Γ_λ is differentiable with injective derivative at every point of B^λ and injective on B^λ), gives, using areaJacobianAt Γ_λ z = normDet(DG(b + λz)) = JG(b + λz) and Hⁿ = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ:
 ∫_{η_{x,λ}(N)} f dHⁿ = ∫_{B^λ} JG(b + λz) f(Γ_λ(z)) dz = ∫_{ℝⁿ} F_λ(z) dz, where F_λ := 1_{B^λ}·JG(b + λ·)·(f ∘ Γ_λ).
 F_λ is measurable (continuous on the open set B^λ and zero outside it).
6. Uniform support and bound (parent 3c). If F_λ(z) ≠ 0 then z ∈ B^λ and |Γ_λ(z)| ≤ R, i.e. |G(b + λz) − G(b)| ≤ λR; the lower bound (both b and b + λz lie in B) gives σλ|z| ≤ λR, so |z| ≤ R/σ. With J_max := the maximum of the continuous function JG over the compact set B_r(c), we get |F_λ| ≤ M_f·J_max·1_{B_{R/σ}(0)} for every λ > 0: an integrable bound independent of λ.
7. Pointwise convergence (parent 3d). Fix z ∈ ℝⁿ. Since B is open and b ∈ B, b + λz ∈ B for all small λ > 0, so 1_{B^λ}(z) → 1. By differentiability of G at b, Γ_λ(z) = (G(b + λz) − G(b))/λ → Lz, hence f(Γ_λ(z)) → f(Lz) (f is continuous). By continuity of JG, JG(b + λz) → JG(b) =: J_L. Thus F_λ(z) → J_L·f(Lz).
8. Dominated convergence (parent 3e). The filter of λ → 0+ (𝓝[>] 0) is countably generated, so tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence yields ∫_{η_{x,λ}(N)} f dHⁿ → J_L ∫_{ℝⁿ} f(Lz) dz.
9. Linear area formula. L is injective, so L is measure preserving from J_L·(Hⁿ on ℝⁿ) to Hⁿ⌞P (SimonGMT Chapter02.measurePreserving_linearMap_normDet_smul, with normDet L = J_L). Hence ∫_P f dHⁿ = J_L ∫_{ℝⁿ} f(Lz) dz. Together with finrank P = n (step 3) this is exactly Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N (G b) (LinearMap.range (DG(b))), which is (iii). ∎
proof_key_steps: Trivial if r ≤ 0; G injective on B by the lower bound
G Lipschitz on B (bounded continuous derivative) gives Hⁿ(N) < ∞; Lusin–Souslin gives N Borel
finrank DG(b)(ℝⁿ) = n
Rescaled parametrization Γ_λ of η_{G(b),λ}(N) on B^λ with DΓ_λ(z) = DG(b + λz)
Area formula: ∫_{η(N)} f = ∫ 1_{B^λ}(z) JG(b + λz) f(Γ_λ z) dz
Uniform support in B_{R/σ}(0) from the lower bound and a λ-independent bound; pointwise limit J_L f(Lz)
Dominated convergence and the linear area formula identify the limit with ∫_P f dHⁿ

subproblems.title: Upper density theorem in μHE[n] form (Simon Ch. 1, Thm 3.6)
subproblems.statement: Let n, ℓ ≥ 0, ν a measure on (the Borel σ-algebra of) ℝ^{n+ℓ} = Amb n ℓ, and A ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} a Borel set with ν(A) < ∞. Then for Hⁿ-almost every x ∈ ℝ^{n+ℓ} (Hⁿ = μHE[n]) with x ∉ A, ν(A ∩ B_r(x))/rⁿ → 0 in [0, ∞] as r ↓ 0 (B_r(x) the closed ball; rⁿ read as ENNReal.ofReal (rⁿ)). (Simon Ch. 1, Upper Density Theorem 3.6, i.e. the cited fact (H2) of the parent proof, in Mathlib's normalization of Hⁿ.)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (ν : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) (A : Set (Amb n ℓ)), MeasurableSet A → ν A < ⊤ → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)), x ∉ A → Tendsto (fun r : ℝ => ν (A ∩ closedBall x r) / ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ n)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 1, Upper Density Theorem 3.6 (cited fact (H2) of the parent proof), through its SimonGMT formalization, translated to Mathlib's normalization μHE[n].

Notation. ℝ^{n+ℓ} = Amb n ℓ (a metric space with its Borel σ-algebra), Hⁿ = μHE[n], B_r(x) is the closed ball. ω_n := Chapter01.realUnitBallVolume (n : ℝ), which lies in (0, ∞) (Chapter01.realUnitBallVolume_pos, Chapter01.realUnitBallVolume_ne_top).

Proof.
1. Borel regularity. μ := ν.toOuterMeasure is Borel regular in Simon's sense (SimonGMT Chapter01.measure_toOuterMeasure_isBorelRegular): Borel sets are μ-measurable and every set has a Borel hull of the same measure. A is Borel, hence Carathéodory-measurable for μ (le_toOuterMeasure_caratheodory), and μ(A) = ν(A) < ∞.
2. Upper Density Theorem. SimonGMT Chapter01.ae_dimensionalUpperDensity_eq_zero_outside (Simon 3.6), applied to μ with the real dimension (n : ℝ) ≥ 0, gives: for simonHausdorffMeasureReal n–almost every x, if x ∉ A then dimensionalUpperDensity μ n A x = limsup_{r↓0} q_x(r) = 0, where q_x(r) := μ(A ∩ B_r(x)) / (ω_n · ofReal(r)^(n:ℝ)).
3. Normalization. SimonGMT Chapter02.simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_smul_euclideanHausdorffMeasure gives simonHausdorffMeasureReal n = c_n • Hⁿ with c_n := Chapter02.simonAreaNormalization n and 0 < c_n < ∞ (simonAreaNormalization_pos, simonAreaNormalization_ne_top). Hence a set is null for one of these measures iff it is null for the other, and the almost-everywhere statement of step 2 holds Hⁿ-almost everywhere.
4. From limsup to limit. Fix x ∉ A at which step 2 holds. Since q_x ≥ 0 and limsup_{r↓0} q_x(r) = 0, also liminf_{r↓0} q_x(r) = 0, so q_x(r) → 0 as r ↓ 0. For r > 0 we have ofReal(r)^(n:ℝ) = ofReal(rⁿ) (ENNReal.ofReal_rpow_of_pos and Real.rpow_natCast), hence ν(A ∩ B_r(x))/ofReal(rⁿ) = ω_n · q_x(r), using ω_n ≠ 0 and ω_n ≠ ∞. Therefore ν(A ∩ B_r(x))/ofReal(rⁿ) → ω_n · 0 = 0 as r ↓ 0 (ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul, ω_n ≠ ∞). This holds for Hⁿ-almost every x ∉ A. ∎
proof_key_steps: ν.toOuterMeasure is Borel regular and A is Carathéodory-measurable with finite measure
SimonGMT Upper Density Theorem 3.6 (a.e. form w.r.t. Simon's Hausdorff measure)
Simon's Hausdorff measure is a positive finite multiple of μHE[n], so the null sets agree
limsup = 0 of a nonnegative quotient gives convergence to 0; rescale by ω_n and identify ofReal(r)^(n:ℝ) = ofReal(rⁿ)

subproblems.title: Locality of approximate tangent planes (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2), Thm 1.6 ⇒)
subproblems.statement: Let n, ℓ ≥ 0, A, N ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} Borel with Hⁿ(A) < ∞ and Hⁿ(N) < ∞ (Hⁿ = μHE[n]), and P a map from ℝ^{n+ℓ} to linear subspaces such that, for every x ∈ N, P(x) is the approximate tangent space of N at x (Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.4; Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N x (P x)). Then for Hⁿ-almost every x ∈ A ∩ N, P(x) is the approximate tangent space of A at x. (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2) / proof of Theorem 1.6 '⇒'.)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (A N : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (P : Amb n ℓ → Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ)), MeasurableSet A → MeasurableSet N → (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) A < ⊤ → (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) N < ⊤ → (∀ x ∈ N, Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N x (P x)) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)).restrict (A ∩ N), Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x (P x)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the parent proof's step 4 (Simon Ch. 3, printed proof of Theorem 1.6 '⇒' and Remark 1.5(2)), with the documented correction: the printed proof applies the upper-density estimate to 'M ∖ N_j', but its displayed decomposition ∫_{η(M)} = ∫_{η(N_j)} − ∫_{η(N_j∖M_j)} + ∫_{η(M∖M_j)} needs it for M ∖ M_j and N_j ∖ M_j. Here A plays the role of M (resp. M_j) and N the role of N_j, and the estimate is applied to A ∖ N and N ∖ A.

Notation. ℝ^{n+ℓ} = Amb n ℓ, Hⁿ = μHE[n], B_r(x) closed ball, η_{x,λ}(y) := λ^(−1)(y − x) = Chapter03.blowUpMap x λ y. For S ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} and a subspace Q, 'T_xS = Q' means Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S x Q: finrank Q = n and ∫_{η_{x,λ}(S)} f dHⁿ → ∫_Q f dHⁿ as λ ↓ 0 for every compactly supported continuous f. The sibling upper_density_zero states: for a measure ν and a Borel set S with ν(S) < ∞, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∉ S, ν(S ∩ B_s(x))/ofReal(sⁿ) → 0 as s ↓ 0.

Proof.
1. Density estimates. A ∖ N and N ∖ A are Borel, with Hⁿ(A ∖ N) ≤ Hⁿ(A) < ∞ and Hⁿ(N ∖ A) ≤ Hⁿ(N) < ∞. The sibling upper_density_zero with ν := Hⁿ gives: for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∉ A ∖ N, Hⁿ((A ∖ N) ∩ B_s(x))/ofReal(sⁿ) → 0, and for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∉ N ∖ A, Hⁿ((N ∖ A) ∩ B_s(x))/ofReal(sⁿ) → 0 (s ↓ 0). A point of A ∩ N belongs to neither A ∖ N nor N ∖ A; as A ∩ N is Borel (ae_restrict_iff'), both limits therefore hold for Hⁿ⌞(A ∩ N)-almost every x. Fix such an x ∈ A ∩ N.
2. Decomposition. Fix a compactly supported continuous f, R > 0 with f = 0 outside B_R(0), M_f := sup|f|, and λ > 0. η := η_{x,λ} is a homeomorphism, so it maps Borel sets to Borel sets and preserves disjointness: η(A) = η(A ∩ N) ⊔ η(A ∖ N) and η(N) = η(A ∩ N) ⊔ η(N ∖ A). By Hausdorff scaling (SimonGMT Chapter04.hausdorff_blowUp_image) Hⁿ(η(S)) = λ^(−n)·Hⁿ(S) < ∞ for every S ⊆ A ∪ N, so the bounded continuous f is integrable on each of these sets, and additivity of the integral over disjoint measurable sets gives
 ∫_{η(A)} f dHⁿ = ∫_{η(N)} f dHⁿ − ∫_{η(N∖A)} f dHⁿ + ∫_{η(A∖N)} f dHⁿ.
3. Error terms. For S ∈ {A ∖ N, N ∖ A}, since f vanishes outside B_R(0),
 |∫_{η(S)} f dHⁿ| ≤ M_f·Hⁿ(η(S) ∩ B_R(0)) = M_f·λ^(−n)·Hⁿ(S ∩ B_{λR}(x)) (SimonGMT Chapter04.hausdorff_blowUp_ball) = M_f·Rⁿ·Hⁿ(S ∩ B_{λR}(x))/(λR)ⁿ,
 which tends to 0 as λ ↓ 0 by step 1 (with s = λR ↓ 0).
4. Conclusion. By hypothesis (x ∈ N), ∫_{η(N)} f dHⁿ → ∫_{P(x)} f dHⁿ. With steps 2–3, ∫_{η(A)} f dHⁿ → ∫_{P(x)} f dHⁿ for every compactly supported continuous f. Also finrank P(x) = n by the hypothesis at x ∈ N. Hence Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x (P x) holds for Hⁿ⌞(A ∩ N)-almost every x. ∎
proof_key_steps: Upper density zero (sibling) for A ∖ N and N ∖ A, hence both density estimates a.e. on A ∩ N
Disjoint decomposition of η(A) and η(N); integrability from Hausdorff scaling
Error integrals bounded by M_f Rⁿ Hⁿ(S ∩ B_{λR}(x))/(λR)ⁿ → 0
Hence ∫_{η(A)} f → ∫_{P(x)} f, i.e. T_xA = P(x)

subproblems.title: Weighted tangent plane from the tangent plane of a Lusin compact (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(1))
subproblems.statement: Let n, ℓ ≥ 0, U ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} open, and V = v(M, θ) a rectifiable n-varifold in U (contract structure RectifiableVarifold; M = V.carrier, θ = V.mult, μ_V = V.weight). Let K ⊆ M be compact with θ continuous on K, x ∈ K, and P a linear subspace which is the approximate tangent space of K at x (Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.4). Assume that for every R > 0, μ_V((M ∖ K) ∩ B_{Rλ}(x))/λⁿ → 0 in [0, ∞] as λ ↓ 0 (closed balls). Then P is the approximate tangent space of M with respect to θ at x (Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.7; Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x P). (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(1).)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)), IsOpen U → ∀ (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (K : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (x : Amb n ℓ) (P : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ)), IsCompact K → K ⊆ V.carrier → x ∈ K → ContinuousOn V.mult K → (∀ R : ℝ, 0 < R → Tendsto (fun r : ℝ => V.weight ((V.carrier \ K) ∩ closedBall x (R * r)) / ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ n)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0)) → Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n K x P → Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n V.carrier V.mult x P
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the parent proof's step 5e (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(1), with the boundedness from Remark 1.5(3)), with details filled in.

Notation. M := V.carrier, θ := V.mult, μ := V.weight = (Hⁿ⌞M) with density ofReal ∘ θ; ℝ^{n+ℓ} = Amb n ℓ, Hⁿ = μHE[n], B_r(y) closed ball, η_λ := η_{x,λ}, η_{x,λ}(y) = λ^(−1)(y − x) = Chapter03.blowUpMap x λ y; C_c denotes the compactly supported continuous real functions. The contract's structure fields give: M ⊆ U, M is Hⁿ-null-measurable, θ > 0 on M, θ is AE-measurable for Hⁿ⌞M, and θ is Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ K' for every compact K' ⊆ U. 'T_xK = P' means Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n K x P (finrank P = n and ∫_{η_λ(K)} f dHⁿ → ∫_P f dHⁿ for every f ∈ C_c). W(x, P) means Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x P: finrank P = n and, for every f ∈ C_c, ∫_{η_λ(M)} f(y)θ(x + λy) dHⁿ(y) → θ(x)∫_P f dHⁿ as λ ↓ 0.

Proof.
1. finrank P = n, because T_xK = P.
2. Local integrability. x ∈ K ⊆ M ⊆ U and U is open; fix ρ > 0 with B_ρ(x) ⊆ U. Then θ is Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ B_ρ(x) and on M ∩ K = K (integrableOn_mult). θ is continuous and positive on the nonempty compact K, so θ ≥ c > 0 on K (IsCompact.exists_isMinOn) and c·Hⁿ(K) ≤ ∫_K θ dHⁿ < ∞; thus Hⁿ(K) < ∞. K is closed, hence Borel.
3. Change of variables (H1). For λ > 0, every function g and every set S ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ}:
 ∫_{η_λ(S)} g(y)θ(x + λy) dHⁿ(y) = λ^(−n) ∫_S g(η_λ(z))θ(z) dHⁿ(z),
 because the push-forward of Hⁿ⌞η_λ(S) under the homeomorphism y ↦ x + λy equals λ^(−n)·Hⁿ⌞S (SimonGMT Chapter04.map_inverse_blowUp_carrier, with Chapter04.blowUpHomeomorph), followed by MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map and integral_smul_measure; this identity of Bochner integrals requires no integrability. The same identity holds with θ replaced by the constant 1.
4. Splitting. Fix f ∈ C_c, R > 0 with f = 0 outside B_R(0), M_f := sup|f|, and 0 < λ < ρ/R. The function h_λ(z) := f(η_λ(z))θ(z) vanishes for z ∉ B_{λR}(x), and |h_λ| ≤ M_f·θ on M ∩ B_{λR}(x) ⊆ M ∩ B_ρ(x); h_λ is AE-strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M; hence h_λ is integrable on M. Writing M as the disjoint union of the Borel set K and M ∖ K, and θ(z) = θ(x) + (θ(z) − θ(x)) on K, step 3 gives
 ∫_{η_λ(M)} f(y)θ(x + λy) dHⁿ(y) = λ^(−n)∫_M h_λ dHⁿ = I_1 + I_2 + I_3, where
 I_1 := θ(x)·λ^(−n)∫_K f(η_λ(z)) dHⁿ(z) = θ(x)∫_{η_λ(K)} f dHⁿ,
 I_2 := λ^(−n)∫_K f(η_λ(z))(θ(z) − θ(x)) dHⁿ(z),
 I_3 := λ^(−n)∫_{M∖K} f(η_λ(z))θ(z) dHⁿ(z);
 all three integrands are integrable (bounded by multiples of 1_K or of θ·1_{M ∩ B_ρ(x)}, using Hⁿ(K) < ∞ and step 2).
5. I_1 → θ(x)∫_P f dHⁿ, by T_xK = P.
6. I_3 → 0. |I_3| ≤ M_f·λ^(−n)∫_{(M∖K) ∩ B_{λR}(x)} θ dHⁿ ≤ M_f·λ^(−n)·μ((M ∖ K) ∩ B_{Rλ}(x)), because ∫_S ofReal ∘ θ d(Hⁿ⌞M) ≤ μ(S) for every set S (withDensity_apply_le) and θ > 0 on M. By hypothesis μ((M ∖ K) ∩ B_{Rλ}(x))/ofReal(λⁿ) → 0 in [0, ∞]; hence it is finite for small λ and its real value tends to 0. So I_3 → 0.
7. I_2 → 0. Let ω(s) := sup{|θ(z) − θ(x)| : z ∈ K ∩ B_s(x)}; ω(s) → 0 as s ↓ 0 because θ restricted to K is continuous at x. Then |I_2| ≤ M_f·ω(λR)·λ^(−n)Hⁿ(K ∩ B_{λR}(x)). The last factor stays bounded (Remark 1.5(3)): λ^(−n)Hⁿ(K ∩ B_{λR}(x)) = Hⁿ(η_λ(K) ∩ B_R(0)) (SimonGMT Chapter04.hausdorff_blowUp_ball) ≤ ∫_{η_λ(K)} g dHⁿ, where g(y) := min{1, max{0, 2 − |y|/R}} is in C_c with 0 ≤ g ≤ 1 and g = 1 on B_R(0); and ∫_{η_λ(K)} g dHⁿ → ∫_P g dHⁿ < ∞ by T_xK = P. Hence the last factor is bounded for small λ and I_2 → 0.
8. By steps 4–7, ∫_{η_λ(M)} f(y)θ(x + λy) dHⁿ(y) → θ(x)∫_P f dHⁿ for every f ∈ C_c; together with step 1 this is W(x, P). ∎
proof_key_steps: finrank P = n; local integrability of θ near x; Hⁿ(K) < ∞ from min θ > 0 on K
Change of variables (H1) via map_inverse_blowUp_carrier, valid for arbitrary sets and integrands
For small λ split the weighted blow-up integral into I_1 + I_2 + I_3 (all integrable)
I_1 → θ(x)∫_P f by T_xK = P
I_3 → 0 by the density hypothesis on μ_V((M ∖ K) ∩ B_{Rλ}(x))
I_2 → 0 by continuity of θ|K at x and the bound λ^(−n)Hⁿ(K ∩ B_{λR}(x)) ≤ ∫_{η(K)} g → ∫_P g

subproblems.title: Continuity of the orthogonal projection onto the range of an injective linear map
subproblems.statement: Let n, ℓ ≥ 0. The map sending a continuous linear map L : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+ℓ} (ℝⁿ = Rn n, ℝ^{n+ℓ} = Amb n ℓ) to the orthogonal projection of ℝ^{n+ℓ} onto its range L(ℝⁿ) (Submodule.starProjection of LinearMap.range L) is continuous on the set of injective L, for the operator-norm topologies.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ), ContinuousOn (fun L : Rn n →L[ℝ] Amb n ℓ => (LinearMap.range L.toLinearMap).starProjection) {L : Rn n →L[ℝ] Amb n ℓ | Function.Injective L}
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the parent proof's step 8a (for injective L, the orthogonal projection onto L(ℝⁿ) is L(LᵀL)^(−1)Lᵀ, which depends continuously on L), with details filled in.

Notation. ℝⁿ = Rn n and ℝ^{n+ℓ} = Amb n ℓ are finite-dimensional real inner product spaces; L† := ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint L; p_S := S.starProjection is the orthogonal projection onto a subspace S; End(ℝⁿ) := ℝⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝⁿ is a complete normed ring; Ring.inverse is the inverse on units and 0 elsewhere.

Proof.
1. The set 𝓘 := {L : ℝⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝ^{n+ℓ} | L injective} is open (ContinuousLinearMap.isOpen_injective; ℝⁿ is finite-dimensional).
2. For L ∈ 𝓘 let A_L := L† ∘ L ∈ End(ℝⁿ). For v ≠ 0, ⟨A_L v, v⟩ = ⟨Lv, Lv⟩ = |Lv|² > 0, so A_L is injective, hence bijective (finite dimension), hence a unit of End(ℝⁿ).
3. Define Q_L := L ∘ Ring.inverse(A_L) ∘ L† : ℝ^{n+ℓ} →L[ℝ] ℝ^{n+ℓ}. For L ∈ 𝓘 and w ∈ ℝ^{n+ℓ}: Q_L w = L(A_L^(−1) L† w) ∈ L(ℝⁿ), and for every v ∈ ℝⁿ, ⟨w − Q_L w, Lv⟩ = ⟨L†w − L†L A_L^(−1) L†w, v⟩ = ⟨L†w − L†w, v⟩ = 0. So w − Q_L w is orthogonal to L(ℝⁿ), and Q_L w = p_{L(ℝⁿ)} w (Submodule.eq_starProjection_of_mem_of_inner_eq_zero). Thus Q_L = p_{L(ℝⁿ)} for all L ∈ 𝓘.
4. Continuity of Q at L₀ ∈ 𝓘. L ↦ L† is continuous (the adjoint is a linear isometric equivalence), and composition of continuous linear maps is jointly continuous, so L ↦ A_L is continuous. Ring.inverse is continuous at the unit A_{L₀} (NormedRing.inverse_continuousAt). Hence L ↦ Q_L = L ∘ Ring.inverse(A_L) ∘ L† is continuous at L₀.
5. For L₀ ∈ 𝓘, the map L ↦ p_{L(ℝⁿ)} agrees with Q on 𝓘 and Q is continuous at L₀, so L ↦ p_{L(ℝⁿ)} is continuous within 𝓘 at L₀ (ContinuousAt.continuousWithinAt and ContinuousWithinAt.congr, using p_{L₀(ℝⁿ)} = Q_{L₀}). Hence the map is ContinuousOn 𝓘. ∎
proof_key_steps: Injective maps form an open set
A_L = L†L is a unit of End(ℝⁿ) for injective L
Q_L = L ∘ A_L^(−1) ∘ L† equals the orthogonal projection onto L(ℝⁿ)
L ↦ Q_L is continuous at injective L (adjoint, composition, NormedRing.inverse_continuousAt)
ContinuousOn by congruence on the set of injective maps

subproblems.title: Lusin compact exhaustion of a rectifiable varifold's carrier (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(1))
subproblems.statement: Let n, ℓ ≥ 0, U ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} open, and V = v(M, θ) a rectifiable n-varifold in U (contract structure RectifiableVarifold; M = V.carrier, θ = V.mult). Then there are compact sets K_m ⊆ M (m ∈ ℕ) such that θ is continuous on each K_m, Hⁿ(K_m) < ∞, and Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_m K_m) = 0 (Hⁿ = μHE[n]). (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(1), first assertion.)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)), IsOpen U → ∀ (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U), ∃ K : ℕ → Set (Amb n ℓ), (∀ m, IsCompact (K m)) ∧ (∀ m, K m ⊆ V.carrier) ∧ (∀ m, ContinuousOn V.mult (K m)) ∧ (∀ m, (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) (K m) < ⊤) ∧ (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) (V.carrier \ ⋃ m, K m) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the parent proof's steps 1 and 5a–5c (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(1), first assertion, which uses Lusin's Theorem, Simon Ch. 1, 1.17), adapted to integrability of θ only on compact subsets of U.

Notation. M := V.carrier, θ := V.mult, μ := V.weight = (Hⁿ⌞M) with density ofReal ∘ θ, so that μ(S) = ∫_{S∩M} θ dHⁿ for Borel S; ℝ^{n+ℓ} = Amb n ℓ, Hⁿ = μHE[n]. The contract's structure fields give: M ⊆ U, M is Hⁿ-null-measurable, θ > 0 on M, θ is AE-measurable for Hⁿ⌞M, and θ is Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ K' for every compact K' ⊆ U.

Proof.
1. Compact exhaustion of U. For i ∈ ℕ let Q_i := {x : |x| ≤ i and Metric.infEDist x Uᶜ ≥ 1/(i + 1)} (with infEDist x ∅ = ∞). Q_i is closed (Metric.continuous_infEDist) and bounded, hence compact. Q_i ⊆ U, since x ∉ U means x ∈ Uᶜ and then infEDist x Uᶜ = 0. ⋃_i Q_i = U: for x ∈ U, x ∉ closure(Uᶜ) = Uᶜ, so infEDist x Uᶜ > 0 (Metric.infEDist_pos_iff_notMem_closure), and both defining conditions hold for all large i.
2. A Borel good part of M. Let θ̃ be a Borel function with θ = θ̃ (Hⁿ⌞M)-almost everywhere (aemeasurable_mult.mk). As M is Hⁿ-null-measurable, Hⁿ(M ∩ {θ ≠ θ̃}) = 0. Choose a Borel M' ⊆ M with Hⁿ(M ∖ M') = 0 (nullMeasurableSet_carrier with NullMeasurableSet.exists_measurable_subset_ae_eq) and a Borel Hⁿ-null set T ⊇ M ∩ {θ ≠ θ̃} (toMeasurable), and set M'' := M' ∖ T. Then M'' is Borel, M'' ⊆ M, θ = θ̃ on M'', and Hⁿ(M ∖ M'') = 0.
3. Finite measures. μ(Q_i) = ∫_{M∩Q_i} θ dHⁿ < ∞ by integrableOn_mult (Q_i is compact and Q_i ⊆ U). So ν_i := μ⌞Q_i is a finite Borel measure on a metric space, hence weakly regular (MeasureTheory.Measure.WeaklyRegular.of_pseudoMetrizableSpace_of_isFiniteMeasure): every Borel set of finite ν_i-measure contains closed subsets of almost full measure (MeasurableSet.exists_isClosed_diff_lt).
4. Lusin. For i, m ∈ ℕ apply SimonGMT Chapter01.exists_isClosed_continuousOn_of_measurable (Simon 1.17) with ν = ν_i, the Borel set A_i := M'' ∩ Q_i (ν_i(A_i) < ∞), the Borel function θ̃ and ε = 1/(m + 1): there is a closed C_{i,m} ⊆ A_i with ν_i(A_i ∖ C_{i,m}) < 1/(m + 1) on which θ̃ is continuous.
5. Properties of C_{i,m}. It is compact (a closed subset of the compact Q_i), and C_{i,m} ⊆ M'' ⊆ M. Since θ = θ̃ on C_{i,m}, θ is continuous on C_{i,m}. If C_{i,m} ≠ ∅, θ is continuous and positive on the compact C_{i,m}, so θ ≥ c > 0 there (IsCompact.exists_isMinOn) and c·Hⁿ(C_{i,m}) ≤ ∫_{C_{i,m}} θ dHⁿ = μ(C_{i,m}) ≤ μ(Q_i) < ∞; hence Hⁿ(C_{i,m}) < ∞ (trivially also when C_{i,m} = ∅).
6. Null remainder. S_i := A_i ∖ ⋃_m C_{i,m} is Borel with S_i ⊆ M ∩ Q_i, and μ(S_i) = ν_i(S_i) ≤ ν_i(A_i ∖ C_{i,m}) < 1/(m + 1) for every m, so 0 = μ(S_i) = ∫_{S_i} ofReal ∘ θ dHⁿ. Since θ > 0 on S_i, this forces Hⁿ(S_i) = 0 (lintegral_eq_zero_iff'). Because M ⊆ U = ⋃_i Q_i, every x ∈ M'' lies in some A_i, so M ∖ ⋃_{i,m} C_{i,m} ⊆ (M ∖ M'') ∪ ⋃_i S_i, which is Hⁿ-null.
7. Enumeration. Let K_k := C_{i,m} where (i, m) := Nat.unpair k. Each K_k is compact, K_k ⊆ M, θ is continuous on K_k, Hⁿ(K_k) < ∞, and Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_k K_k) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Compact exhaustion Q_i of U via Metric.infEDist
Borel representative θ̃ and a Borel M'' ⊆ M of full Hⁿ-measure in M with θ = θ̃ on M''
Finite, weakly regular measures ν_i = μ_V⌞Q_i
SimonGMT Lusin: closed C_{i,m} ⊆ M'' ∩ Q_i, compact, θ continuous on them, Hⁿ(C_{i,m}) < ∞
Null remainder: μ_V(S_i) = 0 and θ > 0 give Hⁿ(S_i) = 0
Enumerate the countable family by Nat.unpair
